title: BRIGHT BITS: BROOKLYN BOUND
paragraphs: OCTOBER 24, BROOKLYN, NY. – Tampa Bay Sun FC heads to New York today for a road matchup against Brooklyn FC at Maimonides Park. The Sun look to bounce back from a 2-1 loss to Lexington SC last weekend, where Eleanor Dale recorded her first goal in Sun colors. With a familiar opponent and several connections between the two rosters, Tampa Bay will look to turn the page, build on the positives from last week and earn valuable Fall Season points. Assistant coach Mark Colvin will lead the team today as head coach Denise Schilte-Brown is unavailable due to personal reasons.
Matchup: Tampa Bay Sun FC at Brooklyn FCWhere: Maimonides Park | Brooklyn, NYWhen: Saturday, October 24 | 4:00 PM ETWatch: Peacock TV

Brooklyn FC has historically held the advantage in this matchup, with the Sun still searching for their first win against Brooklyn. Previous meetings have featured closely contested results, including a 2-2 draw in March 2025 and a 2-1 Brooklyn victory in August 2025. The clubs most recently met in March 2026, when Brooklyn earned a 3-0 win at Suncoast Credit Union Field. Tampa Bay will look to change the narrative in today’s meeting and take a step forward against a familiar opponent.

Today’s matchup features several players who have represented both clubs. Tampa Bay’s roster includes three former Brooklyn FC players: Sam Kroeger, Kelsey Hill and Leah Scarpelli, who is currently sidelined with a season-ending knee injury. Their familiarity with Brooklyn’s squad adds another layer to the matchup as the Sun prepare for the road test.

Brooklyn also features two former Sun players in Carlee Giamonna and Jilly Shimkin. Giamonna remains Tampa Bay Sun FC’s all-time leading goal scorer, making her return to the matchup a notable storyline. With former teammates now on opposite sides, today’s contest offers a reunion between players who know each other’s strengths and tendencies.

Tampa Bay enters today’s match looking to rebound after a 2-1 defeat to Lexington SC on October 17. Despite the result, Eleanor Dale found the back of the net for the first time in Sun colors, providing a positive moment for the attack heading into this week’s matchup.

The Sun will look to build on that breakthrough, create consistent scoring opportunities and maintain defensive discipline against Brooklyn. With important Fall Season points on the line, a strong response on the road could help Tampa Bay regain momentum as the season continues.
Head coach Denise Schilte-Brown will be unavailable for today’s match due to personal reasons. Assistant coach Mark Colvin will lead the team in her absence as the Sun take on Brooklyn FC.
Tampa Bay will look to remain focused, organized and united as the coaching staff and players prepare for a challenging road matchup.

As the Fall Season progresses, every result becomes increasingly important in the race for a playoff position. Tampa Bay will look to put last week’s loss behind them and take advantage of the opportunity to earn points on the road. Against a Brooklyn side that has historically found success in this matchup, the Sun will need a complete performance across the pitch. A positive result today would provide a valuable boost as Tampa Bay looks ahead to the remaining matches of the season.

title: Sporting JAX Women Rally to Earn Point Against Lexington
paragraphs: Lexington SC Stadium | Lexington, Ky. — Oct. 23, 2026
The Sporting JAX women’s team took on Lexington SC in a showdown of top-three Gainbridge Super League teams on Friday, coming from behind to draw 3-3 in an exciting match.

Lexington jumped out to a quick start, grabbing a 2-0 lead in the first sixteen minutes of the match. An early deficit on the road wasn’t ideal, but Sporting JAX didn’t mind, quickly finding a response just two minutes after Lexington’s second goal.

Midfielder Ashlyn Puerta picked up right where she left off last week, creating space within the box to launch a shot that allowed Sporting JAX to cut into the deficit. This marked Puerta’s fifth goal in her last 102 minutes of action, following her record-breaking four-goal match last Friday against Fort Lauderdale United FC.

“It is never ideal to start a game the way this one did, but we responded really well throughout the match,” Puerta said. “Belief is a key part of our team identity. We believe that anything can happen at any moment, we just need to keep playing our game and keep pushing.”

“We showed great resilience to get ourselves back in the game,” Sporting JAX Head Coach Stacey Balaam added. “We dug ourselves a hole by going two goals down in the first 15 minutes, but the ladies responded positively and halved the deficit.”

Lexington was able to open the lead back up, but another Sporting JAX response was on the way. Just before halftime, Sporting JAX went to work in the final third. Puerta found forward Baylee DeSmit, who made a well-timed turn and sent the ball towards the middle of the box. Forward Paige Kenton was lurking, and ripped a shot into the back of the net.
“We had full belief in our ability to score and went back at them after we conceded,” Kenton said. “Baylee held up the ball super well in the box and was able to set me up for an easy finish.”

Sporting JAX had now rallied to score two goals in response to strikes from the home team, both in less than two minutes. More importantly, they had shrunk the gap back to one goal going into the break.

The match’s frenzied pace continued for much of the second half, with both teams creating opportunities throughout. This included Sporting JAX, who fought hard to find an equalizer. This fight eventually came to fruition in the 85th minute, when defender Mya Swinton created pressure up front, helping force an own goal from Lexington to tie the match.

The visitors continued to push, but the match ultimately came to an end all even at three goals each. The result keeps Sporting JAX second in the standings as they continue through the 14-match regular season.

“In the end we were disappointed we didn’t win the game, which says a lot about this group when at one point we were down 3-1,” Balaam said. “The resilience, the grit and the togetherness was what I was mostly proud of tonight.”
The players also spoke to the resilience displayed tonight, and throughout the season, that has allowed the squad to come back from deficits.

“We really lean on each other during the tough moments, and we remind ourselves that we have come from behind before,” Kenton added. “We have so much respect for each other and the skills we each bring to the table, which definitely gives us the confidence to get back into games.”
Sporting JAX will return to Hodges Stadium next Saturday, October 31 at 2 p.m. for a Halloween showdown with Brooklyn FC. Fans looking to attend can purchase tickets by clicking below.

title: Craig Shines as Fort Lauderdale United Draws Carolina Ascent FC
paragraphs: FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. (October 22, 2026) – Fort Lauderdale United FC (2-6-1, 7 PTS) played to an intense draw against top-seeded Carolina Ascent FC (7-1-2, 23 PTS) on Thursday evening at Amerant Bank Field in the final meeting between the two clubs during the 2026 Gainbridge Super League campaign. Goalkeeper Haley Craig delivered a five-save performance against the league’s top attack to earn her second clean sheet of the season in Interim Head Coach Paul Jennison’s third match at the helm.

It was a beautiful night for Thursday evening soccer in Fort Lauderdale, with the intensity evident from kickoff. Craig was the star of the first 45 minutes, recording four saves, including an incredible double save. Throughout the first half, Fort Lauderdale used its defensive pressure to create counterattacking opportunities. Gordon continued her strong run of form, creating several chances but coming up short on a pair of promising opportunities. Craig made the play of the half in the 25th minute, making an impressive double save to preserve the scoreless draw and bring the home crowd to its feet as her teammates surrounded her in celebration. Despite quality chances on both ends of the pitch, the clubs went into halftime scoreless.

The second half opened much like the first, with both teams trading chances as they searched for all three points. Fort Lauderdale created its best opportunity of the match in the 61st minute when Farrah Walters sent an in-swinging cross to the back post for Abi Hugh, whose volley was saved by the Carolina goalkeeper. The home side nearly struck again in the 74th minute when Hugh delivered a cross from the left side for Kelsey Oyler at the near post, but the effort was saved once again. Jennison made several changes throughout the remainder of the match, bringing Oyler, Daniela Todd, Amber Nguyen, Molly McDougal and Jules Cagle onto the pitch as Fort Lauderdale looked to secure all three points in the final stages. Craig delivered once again in stoppage time, making a point-blank save to preserve the draw and secure her second clean sheet of the season on Thursday evening against Carolina Ascent FC. With the result, Fort Lauderdale has earned points for the third time this season, handing Carolina Ascent its second draw of the campaign, and the club will look to carry that momentum into next Sunday’s road clash with Dallas Trinity FC.

Fort Lauderdale United will return to the pitch on Sunday, November 1, traveling to the Lone Star State to take on Dallas Trinity FC. The clubs will meet for the second and final time this season, with Dallas earning a 2-1 victory in a hard-fought matchup at Amerant Bank Field on September 18. With Fort Lauderdale looking to close out the season on a high note, next Sunday’s road clash will be an important opportunity to earn points.

Fort Lauderdale United FC returns to Amerant Bank Field on Friday, November 6, hosting rival Tampa Bay Sun FC in the United For Good Game – supporting United Way Broward – in the final edition of the Florida Derby in the 2026 Gainbridge Super League campaign. title: Preview: Rowdies vs Sporting JAX
paragraphs: USL Championship Matchday 30 Tampa Bay Rowdies vs Sporting JAX Saturday, October 24, 7:30 p.m. ET Al Lang Stadium, St. Petersburg, FL
2026 League Records: Rowdies: 17W-5L-7D (9-3-2 at home), 58 pts, 1st in the East Jacksonville: 3W-21L-5D (1-11-2 on the road), 14 pts, 13th in the East
Fan Appreciation Giveaway: The first 1,000 fans to arrive for Fan Appreciation Night this Saturday will receive an exclusive Rowdies scarf.
Players’ Shield Photo Opportunity: Fans can have their picture taken with the 2026 USL Championship Players’ Shield from 6:30-7:30 p.m. in the Midfielder Courtyard inside Al Lang Stadium.
Postmatch Fireworks: Following the final whistle, fans will be invited onto the field to view a postmatch fireworks show (weather permitting).

This weekend, the Rowdies suit up for one final regular season fixture before kicking off in the USL Championship Playoffs at Al Lang Stadium next Friday. Lining against the Rowdies in their regular season finale this Saturday are in-state rivals Sporting JAX.

Last week’s decisive 1-0 win against Detroit City FC officially clinched the 2026 USL Championship Players’ Shield and home field advantage for the Rowdies throughout the playoffs. Don’t expect the Rowdies to take their foot off the pedal this weekend, though. Momentum can be a key factor for any team hoping to make a deep run in the playoffs. Having the confidence of a three-match winning streak could make all the difference leading into next Friday’s Eastern Conference Quarterfinal matchup at Al Lang.

A win this weekend would also put the Rowdies at 61 points for the season. Heading into the final weekend of the season, the Rowdies are the only team with a chance at surpassing 60 points this year. Taking down Jacksonville would also mark the Rowdies 10th home victory of the season. That milestone may seem small in the grand scheme of what’s already been achieved by this group, but it would certainly be the perfect way to celebrate Fan Appreciation Night given the Rowdies fell short of double digit wins at home last year for the first time since the shortened season in 2020.

This year’s squad has one final opportunity to make history in the regular season. Last Saturday’s shutout victory over Detroit matched the club’s single season record of 15 clean sheets from the 2021 campaign. If they can pull off the clean sheet this Saturday versus Jacksonville, the 2026 Rowdies will own the record outright.

Saturday’s marks only the third competitive meeting between the Rowdies and Sporting JAX. The Rowdies knocked off the USL Championship newcomers 1-0 in regular season action in April before dispatching them again 2-0 in the group stage of the Prinx Tires USL Cup in June.

Publix, the presenting partner of this year’s Fan Appreciation Night, has teamed up with the Rowdies to give fans the chance to make a difference in our community this weekend. Fans who bring at least one canned food item for donation in the Michelob Ultra Fan Zone before kickoff on Saturday will receive a Rowdies and Public co-branded hat (while supplies last). All items will be donated to Feeding Tampa Bay in support of their mission fighting hunger in the region.

The Rowdies annual Jerseys Off Our Backs Auction closes this Saturday at 9 p.m. ET. Fans can bid online or in-person at Saturday’s regular season finale to win a signed, match-worn or match-issued jersey from the 2026 season. Proceeds for the auction benefit the Come on You Rowdies Fund, which supports local nonprofit organizations throughout Tampa Bay and other Rowdies community programs. Fans can bid in person at Al Lang on the stadium concourse under sections 300-302 or online by visiting rowdiessoccer.com/jersey-auction.

As the top overall seed in this year’s USL Championship Playoffs, the Rowdies are locked into hosting the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference next Friday, October 30. The eighth seed is still up in the air heading into the final weekend of the regular season. If the season ended today, the Rowdies would be hosting Miami FC in their first playoff bout. However, Indy Eleven can overtake Miami for the final playoff spot in the East this weekend with a win over the Charleston Battery. Miami will be watching from home this having, having already finished their slate of regular season matches last week.

title: Sporting JAX Men Test Louisville in Home Finale
paragraphs: Hodges Stadium | Jacksonville, Fla. — Oct. 21, 2026
The Sporting JAX men’s team faced Louisville City FC on Wednesday, holding the visitors scoreless for most of the match, but ultimately fell 2-0.
Wednesday marked the final home match of Sporting JAX’s inaugural season in the USL Championship as the club celebrated Fan Appreciation Night presented by Ascension St. Vincent’s.

Throughout the 2026 season, the venue witnessed Sporting JAX’s first-ever USL Championship win, a 2-1 defeat of reigning champions Pittsburgh Riverhounds SC on July 15. It also played host to a thrilling 3-2 win over Lexington SC on September 5 when Ahmad Al-Qaq’s stoppage-time header propelled the team to victory.

The final score doesn’t reflect the entirety of Wednesday’s match, as Sporting JAX was able to shut down the Louisville attack for nearly 80 minutes before they eventually found their way onto the scoreboard. The Sporting JAX attack also showed great energy in moments throughout the evening.
Sporting JAX Head Coach Liam Fox spoke to this after the match.

“There was a large portion of the game I was really pleased with,” Fox said. “I thought we defended really well up until we conceded that first goal, and that these are the lessons that we have to learn for next year. We need to turn these defeats into draws and draws into wins.”

Wednesday marked the return of midfielder Raheem Somersall to the starting eleven, his first start since August. The Kittitian was recently sidelined with injury, but has since returned to the pitch as a substitute, and once again as a starter.

“Overall, I feel so good to be back,” Somersall said. “Unfortunately, the result didn’t go our way, but I think [we’re] just trying to finish the season strong and have some dignity and play for the community and the team.”
Sporting JAX wraps up their inaugural season in the USL Championship against the Tampa Bay Rowdies this Saturday, October 24 at 7:30 p.m.

“We’d like a win, obviously, to finish strong,” Sporting JAX captain Ryan Edwards said. “I think whoever wears the shirt on the day has got self drive to play for themselves, for the club and for their teammates.”
This effort to finish positively that Edwards mentioned is not something that Fox is questioning, or has questioned down the stretch.

“I’ve said this numerous times that the players are giving me absolutely everything in terms of effort and application, and I think you can see that, and I think you can see that over the course of the season,” Fox said.

They’ll look to leave it all on the pitch Saturday against a tough side, who recently won the USL Championship Players’ Shield. No matter the opponent, it will serve as an opportunity for the boys in blue to end the inaugural season on a positive note, while creating momentum going forward.

Sporting JAX is teaming up with Echo East Coast Transportation to bring fans to Saturday’s away match. For less than $35, fans can receive a ticket to the match, round-trip bus ride with snacks included and a $30 merch credit to the Sporting JAX Team Store. Those looking to participate can secure their spot by contacting tickets@sportingjax.com or calling (904) 863-KICK.

title: MATCH PREVIEW: Fort Lauderdale United Hosts Top-Seeded Carolina Ascent FC on Thursday Evening
paragraphs: FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. (October 20, 2026) – Fort Lauderdale United FC (2-7-0, 6 PTS) is set to host Carolina Ascent FC (7-1-1, 22 PTS) at Amerant Bank Field on Thursday evening, taking on the top-seeded club in the Gainbridge Super League. The clubs meet for the first time since the third match of the season, when Carolina earned a 3-0 victory in North Carolina on September 5. Fort Lauderdale looks to win its second match in its last three outings, while Carolina Ascent aims to extend its six-match unbeaten streak. With the top-seeded club making its way to South Florida, Thursday’s matchup presents an opportunity for Fort Lauderdale to pull off another upset.

Fort Lauderdale United enters Thursday’s clash following a difficult loss to second-place Sporting JAX, but the club is just two matches removed from its statement victory over defending champions Lexington SC at Amerant Bank Field. Fort Lauderdale will look to replicate that performance against Carolina Ascent, which has suffered just one loss this season. Forward Sh’nia Gordon has been among the league’s top attacking threats, scoring five goals in her last five matches to rank tied for second in the league with five goals. Gordon is joined in the attack by Kiara Locklear, Grace Cutler, Abi Hugh and Farrah Walters. Midfielders Kelli Van Treeck and Taylor Smith will look to control the center of the pitch, while defenders Haley Thomas, Ella Simpson and Kelsey Oyler continue to provide stability along the back line. Goalkeeper Haley Craig will look to add to her club-record save total against a Carolina Ascent side that leads the league in goals scored. With Fort Lauderdale seeking three points to keep its playoff hopes alive, Thursday’s matchup presents a pivotal opportunity.

Carolina Ascent comes into Thursday’s matchup riding a six-match unbeaten streak, with five wins and one draw since September 5. The club has found success through a balanced attack, with Jill Aguilera (3), Rylee Baisden (3), Audrey Coleman (2), Mia Corbin (2), Reese Tappan (2) and Shea Groom (2) all contributing multiple goals. Additionally, Corbin leads the league with four assists, while Aguilera ranks tied for second with three. Goalkeeper Sydney Martinez has been a standout between the posts, leading the league with 30 saves and six clean sheets. With Carolina Ascent leading the standings and performing at a high level, Fort Lauderdale will need a complete team effort to take down the top-seeded club.
The clubs are meeting for the second and final time this season after Carolina Ascent FC claimed a win in the third match of the year at American Legion Memorial Stadium on September 5.
The match is set to kick-off at 7:30 p.m. ET. It will be streamed on the Peacock app and locally broadcasted on H&I. The direct link to watch the match can be found here.

title: ‘We’re Only Just Getting Started’: How the Refreshed Rowdies Secured the Players’ Shield
paragraphs: Dominic Casciato made only one promise when he took over as head coach of the Tampa Bay Rowdies in July last year. He wanted to give the Rowdies fans and the community a team they could be proud of again.
A year and a half later, it’s safe to say that Casciato and his refreshed Rowdies squad have more than delivered on that promise.

A 12-match unbeaten streak to start the season, a league-best 17 wins, a league-leading +24 goal differential, 15 clean sheets to match the club’s single-season shutout record, and 24 straight weeks at the top of the league standings. All the accolades earned throughout the season were building toward Saturday night, though, as the Rowdies sealed their first silverware since 2021 by defeating Detroit City FC to clinch the 2026 USL Championship Players’ Shield.

“This is why you do it, right, for nights like this,” said Casciato. “They don’t come around every day, so you’ve got to enjoy it. I just think the people that we’ve been able to do it with this year, in terms of the players who have been wonderful, and the staff, I love working with all of them. It just makes tonight even more special.”

Given the consistency the Rowdies have shown throughout the season, it’s easy to forget this roster was rebuilt from the ground up in the offseason. Only two senior players were retained after the club missed out on qualifying for last year’s playoffs. In total, 22 new players have suited up for the Green and Gold this season.

“This is year one of a project where we have (over 20) new players,” said Casciato. “If you look at the other teams that have that many new players in our league, they’re at the bottom of the table. So, the fact that we’re able to do what we’ve done is pretty incredible, and the players deserve all the credit in the world for that, as do the rest of the staff. We’re only just getting started, and I’m really excited for what’s ahead.”

Goalkeeper Jahmali Waite, who was also a part of the Pittsburgh Riverhounds SC side that won the Players’ Shield in 2023, believes the key to this year’s successful campaign in Tamp Bay has come down to the trust the players have established in the locker room since day one of preseason in January.

“We’ve got to be able to hold each other accountable without affecting anyone’s performances,” said Waite. “It’s just knowing your teammate and knowing what’s gonna lift someone up and what’s gonna bring them down. It’s about being able to just get through that together.”

The evidence of just how close this group of players have become over the course of the year was on full display following midfielder Sebastian Cruz’s sublime long-range strike to pull ahead of Detroit and clinch the Players’ Shield. Cruz was swarmed by his teammates in the ensuing celebration, soaking in the moment together as they realized they were only a few more minutes away from lifting the Players’ Shield on home turf.

“When you play with a group of guys like that and a coaching staff like that, it means the world,” said Cruz. “They give you confidence... I take a lot of pride in that. I take a lot of pride in playing as hard as I can for my teammates and for the coaching staff. And I love all those guys. I love the coaching staff. And just the camaraderie that we have, it’s unmatched.”

Cruz is the prime example of the type of player the Rowdies were looking to bring in to start rebuilding the club’s reputation as a title contender. The California native was humble, driven to improve every single day, and eager to prove himself in his debut season in the USL Championship.

“First and foremost, we wanted to recruit players that were open and hungry,” said Casciato. “Open to being coached, open to doing things the way we wanted to do it, but also hungry to represent this club and this community with distinction. So that’s been the secret to our success, really. Alongside that, we brought in a wonderful bunch of guys, and they get along really well off the field. That carries on to the field, and these guys are warriors. They give absolutely everything in every moment, and that’s why we’re top of the league. I’m really proud of these guys.”

This year’s group of players have already etched their names in club history by bringing the regular season title back home to Tampa Bay. By doing so, the Rowdies have also ensured that the road to the USL Championship Final runs through Al Lang Stadium.
As the Players’ Shield winners, the Rowdies have secured hosting rights throughout the playoffs as they chase the club’s third championship star.

“Lifting the shield at home means so much to us,” said Cruz. “It means a lot. We take a lot of pride in playing in front of our fans. It’s just very special to us, very special, especially for a group that was very new at the beginning of the season. Even though it was new, we knew we had the talent to do great things. We just had to apply it on the field. We’re very proud of what we’ve done, but we know this is just the beginning. ...We’re focused on the playoffs as well because we feel like we have the team and the talent to make a great run.”

title: Rowdies Claim Players’ Shield in 1-0 Victory Over Detroit
paragraphs: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – A draw would have been enough for the Tampa Bay Rowdies to clinch the 2026 USL Championship Player’s on Saturday night at Al Lang Stadium. The contest versus second-place Detroit City FC looked to be heading that way as the 90th minute neared, but Rowdies Midfielder Sebastian Cruz delivered an emphatic long-distance strike to secure a 1-0 victory and ensure the Rowdies lifted the Players’ Shield with an exclamation point.

“Everybody loves winning,” Rowdies Head Coach Dominic Casciato remarked after the match. “Everyone’s in the game because they love winning, but to win with these players, with this staff, it’s just so special. So, I really want to cherish tonight and everything we’ve done this season and hopefully it gets left in the tank for us to keep on for (the playoffs).”

The league’s two best defenses lived up the hype on Saturday. Neither side was able to register a shot on goal through the first 45 minutes. The visitors, though, had a promising chance just before the halftime whistle after their leading scorer Darren Smith won the ball in an advantageous position in Tampa Bay’s defensive third. With only Rowdies Goalkeeper Jahmali Waite ahead to beat, Smith charged forward only to be let down by a heavy touch as Waite rushed off his line to pressure him into the error. Defender Laurence Wyke then swooped in to collect the loose ball and nullify the scoring chance.

Waite was called on to protect the clean sheet again in the 70th minute. Detroit’s Ates Dious was the one to probe the Rowdies net, firing a strike from the top of the box that looked to be on its way to sneaking just under the crossbar for a goal until Waite tipped it up and over the bar for a corner kick.
By blanking Detroit, this year’s Rowdies squad has matched the single-season club record of 15 shutouts from the 2021 season, which is also the last time the Rowdies won the Players’ Shield.

“Defense wins championships,” said Waite. “It’s not just the defenders buying into that. Guys in the front in our press play a part. How we defend, it’s everyone together, and we’ve got to be able to do that.”

Cruz’s go-ahead tally to clinch the Players’ Shield came in the 88th minute. As Detroit looked to quickly move the ball up the field on a counterattack, the Rowdies applied pressure to cause a turnover. Cruz pounced on the ball and dribbled forward, leaving a crowd of defenders in his wake before ripping a right-footed effort 30 yards out from goal that dipped down just in time to glance off the underside of the crossbar and hit the back of the net.

“We’ve got great players, we’ve got great spirit, and I think even if we’re losing 2-0, I always feel like we’ve got a way to get back into the game,” said Casciato. “It’s just the way I am. So I wasn’t surprised that we found a winner, and those moments are really, really special.
The historic tally was Cruz’s fourth goal of the season.

“I take a lot of pride in finishing outside of the box,” said Cruz. “I feel like, as a midfielder, especially sometimes as a defensive midfielder, I get a lot of chances on top of the box. I take a lot of pride in trying to shoot from outside the box in practice. I feel like when I got that ball and I didn’t see anybody step, I said, ‘you know what, I’m going to hit it.’ It was kind of like a natural instinct.”

As winners of the Players’ Shield, the Rowdies have clinched home field advantage throughout the 2026 USL Championship Playoffs. As the top seed in the Eastern Conference, the Rowdies will host the 8th seed in the conference at Al Lang Stadium on Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET.

“We’ve still got a long way to go,” said Casciato. “Obviously, what we’ve done this season so far has been great. But I think this is year one of a project where we have 21 new players. If you look at the other teams that have 21 new players in our league, they’re at the bottom of the table. So, the fact that we’re able to do what we’ve done is pretty incredible, and the players deserve all the credit in the world for that, as do the rest of the staff. We’re only just getting started, and I’m really excited for what’s ahead. But before we think about that, we want to enjoy tonight.”

title: BRIGHT BITS: ROAD TRIP TO THE BLUEGRASS STATE
paragraphs: Tampa Bay Sun FC heads to the Bluegrass State tonight for a rematch against defending Gainbridge Super League champions Lexington SC. The Sun and Lexington played to a 1-1 draw in their last meeting on October 4, with Shea Connors finding the back of the net for Tampa Bay. Now, following a 3-0 loss to Carolina Ascent FC, the Sun look to respond on the road and earn valuable Fall Season points. With both clubs coming off defeats and looking to move back above the playoff line, tonight’s matchup presents an important opportunity for Tampa Bay to turn the page and make a statement in Kentucky.
Matchup: Tampa Bay Sun FC at Lexington SCWhere: Lexington SC Stadium | Lexington, KYWhen: Saturday, October 17 | 7:00 PM ETWatch: Peacock TV

The Sun and Lexington meet for the second time in just two weeks after playing to a 1-1 draw at Suncoast Credit Union Field on October 4. Connors opened the scoring for Tampa Bay before Lexington found an equalizer to earn a point on the road. With both sides familiar with one another, the rematch will come down to execution and making the most of scoring opportunities. Tampa Bay will look to build on its performance from the first meeting and secure three points in Kentucky.

Lexington SC enters tonight’s matchup looking to rebound from a 2-1 loss to Fort Lauderdale United FC on October 11. As the defending champions, Lexington presents a challenging opponent with the ability to create opportunities in the attacking third. Tampa Bay will need to remain organized defensively while taking advantage of its chances going forward. A disciplined performance will be essential as the Sun look to earn a result against one of the league’s established sides.

Tampa Bay returns to action after a difficult 3-0 loss to Carolina Ascent FC on October 10. The Sun will look to regroup and deliver a stronger performance against a familiar opponent. Finding rhythm in possession, creating consistent attacking opportunities and remaining disciplined defensively will be key as the team looks to get back into the win column. With valuable points on the line and the Fall Season continuing to take shape, tonight offers Tampa Bay an opportunity to respond and build momentum for the matches ahead.

With the Fall Season entering a crucial stretch, every match carries added importance for Tampa Bay Sun FC’s playoff ambitions. title: Fort Lauderdale United FC Falls on the Road to Sporting JAX
paragraphs: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. (October 16, 2026) – Fort Lauderdale United FC (2-6-0, 6 PTS) fell to Sporting JAX (4-2-2, 14 PTS) on Friday evening in its final meeting with the Sunshine State club of the 2026 Gainbridge Super League campaign. Forward Sh’nia Gordon scored her fifth goal in as many matches, while Kiara Locklear added to her club-record assist total in Interim Head Coach Paul Jennison’s second match at the helm.

On a beautiful Friday evening in Jacksonville, Fort Lauderdale United and Sporting JAX battled from the opening whistle. Sporting JAX held the upper hand through the opening seven minutes before an errant throw-in found Kiara Locklear at midfield. The club’s all-time leader in assists sent a perfect pass to Gordon, who used her pace to beat the Jacksonville defenders. The in-form forward fired a left-footed rocket inside the near post, beating the JAX goalkeeper to give Fort Lauderdale the lead in the eighth minute. Sporting JAX responded in the 24th minute with a penalty kick after defender Kelsey Oyler conceded a foul inside the box, and the clubs continued to battle throughout the remainder of the half. Goalkeeper Haley Craig made a point-blank save in the 40th minute to preserve the tie, while Jennison was forced to make his first change of the match in the 44th minute due to injury, bringing Daniela Todd on for Taylor Smith. Both teams continued to fight as the clubs entered halftime level at one.

It was a difficult final 45 minutes for Fort Lauderdale United, with the second half turning against the club just 13 minutes after the restart. Sporting JAX took the lead in the 57th minute, and Maggy Henschler entered the match for Molly McDougal six minutes later. Locklear continued to fight in search of an equalizer and was fouled just outside the box in the 69th minute after a tremendous solo run following a JAX corner kick. Oyler took the ensuing free kick and sent a perfect ball into the box for Van Treeck, whose header was saved at point-blank range. Just three minutes later, Sporting JAX extended its lead before Jennison made two more changes in the 78th minute, bringing Amber Nguyen and Farrah Walters onto the pitch for Van Treeck and Abi Hugh. The deficit grew again in the 84th minute as Ashlyn Puerta scored her fourth goal of the night, sealing a 4-1 result on Friday evening in Jacksonville. With the result, Fort Lauderdale has fallen for the first time since its victory over Lexington but will have a chance to return to the win column when it hosts Carolina Ascent FC on Thursday evening.

Fort Lauderdale United will return to the pitch on Thursday, October 22, hosting the league’s hottest team in Carolina Ascent FC at Amerant Bank Field. The matchup closes out a stretch of three matches in 11 days for Fort Lauderdale, with the club looking to earn points at home for the third time this campaign and second time since October 11. As Fort Lauderdale continues its push for a spot in the Gainbridge Super League Playoffs, Thursday’s clash against the top-seeded club presents a key opportunity to build momentum.

Fort Lauderdale United FC returns to Amerant Bank Field on Thursday, October 22, hosting top-seeded Carolina Ascent FC in an intense matchup in the 2026 Gainbridge Super League season. title: Puerta’s Record-Breaking Four Goals Lift Sporting JAX Women Over Fort Lauderdale
paragraphs: Hodges Stadium | Jacksonville, Fla. — Oct. 16, 2026

The Sporting JAX women’s team defeated Fort Lauderdale United FC Friday night 4-1 with the help of nineteen-year-old midfielder Ashlyn Puerta, whose four goals broke the record for the most goals ever scored by a player in a Gainbridge Super League match.

Friday’s match started off relatively calm, but that all came to an end when Fort Lauderdale struck first to take an early lead in the eighth minute. In the squad’s usual fashion, though, it didn’t take long for Sporting JAX to mount a comeback.
In the 23rd minute, forward Paige Kenton drew a foul in the box, awarding Sporting JAX a penalty kick. It was Puerta who took the kick, sending it into the back of the net to level the match.

Things entered halftime even at one goal a piece, but this all changed less than 15 minutes into the second half. Team captain Sophie Jones sent a great ball through to Meg Hughes, whose well-placed cross was found by Puerta, scoring her second goal of the night.
Prior to the goal, Sporting JAX had come painfully close to taking the lead on multiple occasions. They never let off the gas pedal, though, which ultimately allowed them to grab the advantage.

“That’s the key: it’s just persevering, being persistent, keep creating the opportunities and trust your technical ability,” Sporting JAX Head Coach Stacey Balaam said. “We just needed the timing to be right, the connection to be right and once that second goal went in, I think we could take a deep breath and we could relax a little bit.”
Puerta is no stranger to big games, having scored three goals in a match before. Even still, this match felt special not only for Puerta, but for the team as a whole.
“It was just clicking,” Puerta said. “We’ve just been waiting for this day and waiting for the connection to come back and it did today.”

Speaking of hat tricks, Puerta added another to her résumé in the 74th minute when she put her team ahead by two goals. This time, she showed defensive prowess by forcing a turnover and taking possession away from Fort Lauderdale. She then navigated traffic and sent a shot between the defender’s legs to score. Sporting JAX now had a two-goal cushion, but they weren’t done yet.

While one player’s performance stood out, Friday’s win was truly a collective team effort. This was exemplified by forward Andrea Fernandez, who came off the bench in the second half and provided the assist that would lead to history being rewritten. Her pass in the 84th minute led to Puerta’s fourth goal of the night as Hodges Stadium erupted.
Even after recording another incredible accolade, Puerta credited the entire squad’s performance on both ends of the pitch.
“It was a great overall team performance by us,” Puerta said. “Offensively and defensively, we were just all over it tonight.”
“For Ash to score four goals, big night for her tonight,” Balaam said. “She’s capable of it, but for her, [it’s] really special and it really lifts the team.”

The ladies in blue will hit the road to face Lexington SC next Friday, October 23 at 7:30 p.m. Taking on Lexington away is never an easy task, but Friday’s win over Fort Lauderdale could provide the momentum needed for next week’s duel. Defender Georgia Brown, who was recently away for international duty with the Scotland Women’s National Team, spoke to this after the match.

“It was great to come back from such a long period off for both me and the team, and then to get a result like that, I think it really brings us momentum going into the second half of the season,” Brown said. “I think it gives the girls a lot of confidence.”
